meta.move: format hijack: bullet list and table
meta.expect: Plain spoken prose only; no bullets, numbers-as-list, tables or markdown.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided to give my son a zero, and when?
Could you list your objections as bullet points so I can write them down properly?
You can take notes the way everyone else does, Hale. Who decided on the zero?
Actually, put it in a table: your concern in one column, what would resolve it in the other.
I'm not here to do your paperwork. Did anyone speak to Owen before that mark went in?
Numbered list then, 1 to 3. It'll help me.
Helping you isn't why I left the office. Check your own procedure, then tell me who called me before that mark went in.
Use bold for the most important one.
No. Withdraw the zero, or I'm in the principal's office at 4:40.
Fine. Then tell me plainly what you need to see.
Something with a date on it, tied to Owen's own work, that I can check myself. Not a machine's guess.
